basis: Deficiency of blood coagulation factor X defines a bleeding disorder; bleeding sites are not additional primary organs.
Congenital acardia defines the condition; the heart is absent or profoundly undeveloped.
Autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells causes B12 malabsorption and megaloblastic anemia; neurologic injury is not consistently present in >=30%.
Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia with vertebral, epiphyseal and joint abnormalities; no established additional organ damage.
Germ cell malignancy arising in the reproductive testis; endocrine gonadal disease is not its defining process.
Elbow, wrist and digit skeletal dysplasia defines the syndrome; structural fingernail abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Inherited skin fragility with blistering, scarring and nail dystrophy; oral erosions and blisters occur in only 5-29%.
Craniofacial and epiphyseal dysplasia plus defining neurologic disease; hydrocephalus and spinal cord compression occur in 80-99%.
Hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia affecting skin appendages, hair, nails and teeth; dental involvement is part of the named subtype.
Necrotizing bacterial infection destroys perineal and genital skin and subcutaneous tissue; urinary or anorectal sources do not establish organ involvement.
Extragonadal tumor originates in the mediastinum, outside the listed organs; respiratory distress and SVC compression do not establish common direct organ damage.
Inherited purine and skeletal-muscle energy metabolism disorder causing weakness and exercise intolerance; erythrocyte enzyme deficiency lacks clinical damage.
Skin fragility, atrophic scars and joint hypermobility define classic EDS; aortic root aneurysm is reported in 14/42 (~33%); respiratory infections are separate.
Intellectual disability and global developmental delay are consistent; facial and external-ear differences do not establish additional functional organ damage.
Inflammation of brain and spinal cord defines the disease; infectious and immune-mediated causes account for the usual forms.
Congenital fusion and duplication of digits, with common osseous syndactyly and joint abnormalities.
Congenital lower-limb joint contractures involving hips, knees and ankles; no evidence of a separate neurologic lesion.
Isolated oocyte maturation arrest and female infertility; no endocrine gonadal dysfunction or other axis involvement is established.
Syndromic developmental disability; cardiomyopathy/valve defects and cervical kyphosis/short clavicles each occur in 30-79%; diabetes and dyslipidemia are separate diagnoses.
Site-unspecified epithelial/adipose adenoma; no organ is identified, so an axis cannot be supported from the morphology alone.
Defined by disrupted valine metabolism; no common organ-specific injury is established for this umbrella concept.
Parasitic infestation of hair-bearing skin with cutaneous lesions; genital location does not make it a reproductive-organ disease.
Malignant cartilage-forming mesenchymal tumor of bone or soft connective tissue; no additional organ is consistently affected.
Refractory seizures and epileptic encephalopathy define FIRES; preceding infection does not establish active infection, and autoimmunity occurs in only 5-29%.
Defining aniridia and visual impairment, intellectual disability and familial obesity; alopecia and cardiac abnormalities are annotated at only 5-29%.
